topIssues.title: op-acceptance-tests: switch to op-reth-only sequencing for Karst+
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Context

op-geth is being deprecated as of the **Karst** fork. The accompanying op-geth change ([op-geth#802](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/802)) adds a kill switch: the beacon consensus engine refuses to build, seal, or import any block whose timestamp activates Karst. Consequently, **op-geth can no longer sequence or verify a Karst chain**, and every acceptance-test path that uses op-geth at Karst+ must move to op-reth (the official Karst EL client, which has full Karst support).

This issue tracks making **op-acceptance-tests sequence and verify on op-reth for Karst+** (op-geth remains valid up to and including Jovian).

## Evidence (from the CI probe)

Draft probe PR [#21167](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21167) repins op-geth to the kill-switch commit. CircleCI `memory-all-*` acceptance results:

| EL variant | Failures | Nature |
|---|---|---|
| `memory-all-opn-op-geth` (op-geth EL) | **93** | Broad — op-geth refuses to seal/import Karst blocks (expected) |
| `memory-all-opn-op-reth` (op-reth EL) | **7** | All in supernode sync-tester + interop follow-L2 |

The 7 op-reth-variant failures were the actionable signal: even with `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-reth`, these tests still spun up an **op-geth** node and hit the kill switch.

Failing tests:
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/sync_tester`: `TestSupernodeVerifierAdvancesViaSyncTester`, `TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsFromCold`, `TestSupernodeVerifierCatchesUpFromCold`, `TestSupernodeVerifierSyncsThroughInteropActivation`, `TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsThroughInteropActivation`
- `op-acceptance-tests/tests/supernode/interop/follow_l2`: `TestFollowSource_P2PSync`, `TestFollowSource_HeadsDivergeThenConverge`

## Root cause: presets that hardcode op-geth

Two devstack constructors called `startL2ELNode` (op-geth) directly instead of the env-aware dispatch `startL2ELForKey` / `startSequencerEL` ([singlechain_build.go#L153](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/singlechain_build.go#L153)):

1. Sync-tester sequencer EL — [singlechain_supernode_synctester_variant.go#L59](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/singlechain_supernode_synctester_variant.go#L59)
2. Follow-L2 follower EL — [multichain_supernode_runtime.go#L515](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/multichain_supernode_runtime.go#L515)

## Approach (decided)

**Karst-aware EL selection + auto-skip op-geth**, implemented at the single EL dispatch point:

1. **De-hardcode op-geth** — route the two spots above through the env-aware dispatch (`startSequencerEL` / `startL2ELForKey`). No behavior change for the op-geth variant; the op-reth variant then truly runs op-reth everywhere.
2. **Karst-aware guard** — in `startL2ELForKey` ([singlechain_build.go#L153](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/singlechain_build.go#L153)) and the mixed-runtime per-node path ([mixed_runtime.go#L182](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go#L182)): when `l2Net.ChainConfig().IsKarst(genesis.Timestamp)` and the requested EL is op-geth, `t.Skipf(...)`; otherwise route to op-reth. Net: **on a Karst-at-genesis chain, no op-geth node is ever started** — op-geth-requested tests skip, everything else sequences/verifies on op-reth. No change for ≤ Jovian chains.

### Resolved investigations
- **op-reth as sequencer**: already first-class in devstack (`MixedL2ELOpReth`), driven by the EL-agnostic batcher + test-sequencer over RPC. No new plumbing.
- **`--builder.interval=100ms` / `--builder.deadline`** ([mixed_runtime.go#L333](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/8a0fb5a914f8023a90baf9dfcd2c6a56515e6326/op-devstack/sysgo/mixed_runtime.go#L333)): confirmed via `op-reth node --help` these are payload-*job* parameters (how a *requested* payload is refined before `getPayload`/deadline), **not** autonomous sealing. The test-sequencer drives blocks via the Engine API, so there is no race and **no op-reth on-demand/test-mode flag is required** for acceptance.

## Local verification

Branch implementing the above, run against a Karst-at-genesis config:

| Test | EL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sync_tester/TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsFromCold` | op-reth | ✅ PASS (op-reth is the sequencer) |
| `sync_tester/TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsFromCold` | op-geth | ⏭️ SKIP (auto-skip fired) |
| `interop/follow_l2/TestFollowSource_P2PSync` | op-reth | ✅ PASS (exercises the follower fix) |

## Acceptance criteria
- With Karst active, no op-geth node is started in any acceptance-test preset/runtime.
- `memory-all-opn-op-reth` and `memory-all-kona-op-reth` are green against a Karst-activated config.
- op-geth coverage for ≤ Jovian is preserved (op-geth variant skips Karst+ tests).

## Out of scope (separate tracks)
- **op-e2e/actions + proofs** — embed op-geth in-process as a Go library; op-reth coverage there is gated on the Rust `op-reth-test-engine` (#20415), which additionally needs *stateful incremental payload building* in op-reth (tx-by-tx). Tracked separately.
- The op-geth kill switch itself ([op-geth#802](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/802)) and the go.mod bump probe ([#21167](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21167)).

topIssues.title: Formalize the ActivationTime/SetActivationTime fork-switch pattern as a shared design
topIssues.author: sebastianst
topIssues.body:
## Context

Two OP-Stack config types now express their hardfork schedule through the same two-method pattern: a single `ActivationTime(fork) *uint64` switch and a paired `SetActivationTime(fork, *uint64)` setter, with `IsForkActive(fork, t)` and every `Is<Fork>` predicate delegating to `ActivationTime`. The fork→field mapping lives in exactly one place per type.

- **`rollup.Config`** — the consensus-layer rollup config:
  - [`ActivationTime`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L581-L614) / [`SetActivationTime`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L616-L649)
  - [`IsForkActive`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L439-L442) and [`ActivateAt`](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/blob/f176635fafcd5e7f6dc07b52e391bdc0c249fda6/op-node/rollup/types.go#L679-L695)
- **`op-core/params.ChainConfig`** — the execution-layer chain config that wraps upstream `params.ChainConfig`, added in #20260 (part of the op-geth decoupling, #20257).

## Problem

The pattern is currently **copy-pasted per type**, with a few sharp edges:

- **Two parallel `switch` statements that must stay in lockstep.** A fork mapped to the wrong field in `ActivationTime` but not `SetActivationTime` (or vice versa) is a silent bug; only a dedicated round-trip test catches it. Each new type re-introduces this risk.
- **Each type re-derives `IsForkActive` and the per-fork predicates**, so the same boilerplate is duplicated.
- **Implementations have already diverged.** `rollup.Config` covers `Delta` and `PectraBlobSchedule` and adds `ActivateAt` / `ActivateAtGenesis` / `IsActivationBlock`; `op-core/params.ChainConfig` omits `Delta` (no execution-layer field for it) and the activation-block helpers. The set of forks each type supports — and how it reports unknown forks — is decided independently.

## Proposal (to design)

Write up the pattern as a formal, reusable design. Options to evaluate:

1. **Shared generic helper / mixin** keyed on `forks.Name` that both types embed, so each type supplies only its fork→field binding once and gets `IsForkActive` + predicates for free.
2. **Code-generate the switches from `forks.All`**, eliminating the lockstep-drift risk entirely and making "add a fork" a single edit.
3. **Documented convention + a shared test helper** that asserts the `ActivationTime`/`SetActivationTime` round-trip for every fork a type claims to support, even if the switches stay hand-written.

Deliverable: a short design doc (e.g. under `docs/ai/` or a `design-docs` entry) capturing the chosen approach and the trade-offs, plus follow-up issues to converge the existing implementations onto it.

## References

- Pattern origin: `rollup.Config` (links above)
- New instance: `op-core/params.ChainConfig` (#20260)
- Epic: op-geth decoupling (#20257)

topPRs.title: fix(kona-host): retry witness fetches via the get_preimage loop, not debug_dbGet
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
`debug_executePayload` (the `L2PayloadWitness` hint) and the `L2BlockData` optimistic-block re-execution are "high-level" hints that bulk-populate the preimage store. They were fetched once when received and then discarded, so any error was terminal — the client fell back to per-node `debug_dbGet`, which op-reth doesn't implement, turning a transient failure into a permanent one.

Rather than introduce a separate retry/backoff path, this plugs them into the **existing `get_preimage` retry loop** (the same one that already retries `debug_dbGet` forever):

- High-level hints are no longer fetched eagerly in `route_hint`; the latest one is **retained**.
- On each `get_preimage` attempt the retained high-level hint is tried **first** (bulk-populating the store), then the fine-grained hints.
- A high-level hint is **cleared once it succeeds** (its response is deterministic, so re-issuing it is pointless) and **kept while it fails**, so a transient error is retried indefinitely — and an unrelated later low-level hint won't re-trigger an already-satisfied high-level fetch.
- Any failure is retried, **including JSON-RPC method-not-found** — it's cheap and lets the fetch start working if the node is upgraded. Even while the high-level fetch keeps failing, each loop attempt still falls through to the fine-grained `debug_dbGet` hint, so nodes that genuinely lack `debug_executePayload` are still served.

### Behavioral change: high-level hints are now lazy

Previously a high-level (proactive) hint was fetched **eagerly and synchronously** in `route_hint` the moment it was received. Now it is only **retained** there and executed lazily by the `get_preimage` loop — i.e. **not until an actual preimage request arrives for a key that isn't already in the store**. If the requested preimage already exists, the loop never runs and the high-level fetch is skipped entirely.

This is functionally equivalent for the proof flow (the witness fetch just shifts from hint-receipt time to the first cache-missing `get_preimage`), and it **avoids redundant executions**: an expensive fetch like `debug_executePayload` or the `L2BlockData` re-execution is no longer re-run when the needed preimages are already available, and is cleared after its first success so subsequent requests don't repeat the identical call.

The `debug_executePayload` call is consolidated into `backend::util::fetch_execution_witness`, de-duplicating the single-chain and interop handlers. `L2BlockData`'s handler body is unchanged — it benefits from the retained-hint retry automatically. Regression coverage lives in `backend::online`'s test module (retry-to-success + clear, high-level-before-fine-grained, fine-grained fallback survival, and route separation).

topPRs.title: fix(op-challenger): tear down VM process group on timeout
topPRs.author: ajsutton
topPRs.body:
The run-trace runner bounds each VM run with `--vm-timeout`, but the timeout did not reliably terminate a wedged run.

The VM (cannon) spawns the oracle/preimage server as its own child, which inherits the VM's stdout/stderr pipes. `exec.CommandContext` only SIGKILLs the direct child on cancellation, so the oracle server is orphaned and keeps the pipe write ends open. `cmd.Wait` then blocks forever waiting for EOF, so the VM timeout never actually tears the run down (we observed a run wedged ~18h despite the 3h default).

Fix: run the VM in its own process group, kill the whole group (negative pid) on cancellation, and set a bounded `WaitDelay` as a backstop so `RunCmd` always returns once the context is cancelled. The process-group bits are Unix-only and guarded behind a build tag with a no-op fallback so cross-compilation still works.

Adds a regression test that spawns a grandchild holding stdout open and asserts `RunCmd` returns promptly and the grandchild is killed.

topPRs.title: chore: additional dependency cleanup
topPRs.author: mds1
topPRs.body:
## Summary

This PR does additional dependency cleanup. It removes direct dependency edges from test/debug surfaces only. It does not touch protocol logic, derivation, proof execution, contracts, generated artifacts, release artifacts, or deployment semantics.

Overall, this removes 2 direct Go requirements. Both modules remain indirect dependencies elsewhere in the repo, so this PR removes 0 unique Go module paths from the full module graph, and the WIZ comparison shows 0 CVEs removed.

## Changes

- Replaces `go-spew` debug dumps in devstack and acceptance-test code with existing structured logging.
- Replaces the Kona Go test websocket helper's direct `gorilla/websocket` source import with the repo's existing `github.com/coder/websocket` dependency.

## Safety / OP Property DB classification

- `go-spew` removal touches `op-devstack` and `op-acceptance-tests`, which are test/developer surfaces. Per the OP Property DB taxonomy, tests and validation surfaces are not automatic Ring 0 unless the PR changes accepted implementation behavior or removes the only critical equivalence/proof coverage. This only changes debug output formatting and preserves the same information via existing loggers.
- Kona websocket cleanup touches `rust/kona/tests/node/utils/ws.go`. While `rust/kona/**/*` is conservatively Ring 0-adjacent because Kona can affect proof execution and accepted proof paths, this file is a Go test helper, not Rust Kona proof/client implementation. The enforcement surface is `tests_validation`, and this PR does not change accepted implementation behavior or remove coverage. The helper keeps the same JSON-RPC subscribe/read/unsubscribe flow while consolidating on an existing websocket dependency.

## Dependency and CVE impact

- Direct `go.mod` requirements: `54 -> 52` (`-2`)
- Full `go list -m all` graph: `540 -> 540` (`0`)
- Fully removed unique module paths: `0`
- Transitive-only fully removed module paths: `0`
- WIZ vulnerability findings: `51 -> 51` (`0`)

`github.com/davecgh/go-spew` and `github.com/gorilla/websocket` are removed as direct requirements/source imports but remain indirect.

topPRs.title: op-devstack: sequence on op-reth for Karst+ in acceptance tests
topPRs.author: sebastianst
topPRs.body:
## Summary

op-geth is being deprecated as of the **Karst** fork and (with [op-geth#802](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/op-geth/pull/802)) refuses to build, seal, or import Karst blocks. This makes the acceptance-test harness sequence and verify Karst-activated chains on **op-reth** — the official Karst EL client — instead of op-geth.

Resolves the op-reth-variant acceptance failures surfaced by the op-geth bump probe ([#21167](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/optimism/pull/21167)), where presets that hardcoded op-geth hit the kill switch even under `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND=op-reth`.

## Changes

- **De-hardcode op-geth** in the two presets that bypassed the env-aware EL dispatch, so they honor `DEVSTACK_L2EL_KIND`:
  - sync-tester sequencer EL (`singlechain_supernode_synctester_variant.go`) → `startSequencerEL`
  - follow-L2 follower EL (`multichain_supernode_runtime.go`) → `startL2ELForKey`
- **Karst-aware guard** at the EL dispatch point (`startL2ELForKey`) and the mixed-runtime per-node path:
  - **env-selected op-geth** on a Karst-at-genesis chain → **skip** (the op-geth CI lane cannot cover Karst; it still runs ≤ Jovian).
  - **explicit `spec.ELKind = op-geth`** on a Karst chain → **fail** (a test misconfiguration).
  - everything else sequences/verifies on op-reth. No change for ≤ Jovian chains.

## Local verification

Run against a Karst-at-genesis config:

| Test | EL | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `sync_tester/TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsFromCold` | op-reth | ✅ PASS (op-reth is the sequencer) |
| `sync_tester/TestSupernodeVerifierELSyncsFromCold` | op-geth | ⏭️ SKIP (auto-skip fired) |
| `interop/follow_l2/TestFollowSource_P2PSync` | op-reth | ✅ PASS (exercises the follower fix) |

## Notes

- This lands ahead of the op-geth kill switch and is independently green: it's keyed on `ChainConfig.IsKarst(genesis)`, so the op-geth lane already skips Karst-activated tests while the op-reth lane runs them.
- Out of scope: `op-e2e/actions`/proofs op-reth coverage, which is gated on the Rust `op-reth-test-engine` (#20415).

Closes #21182.
